{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABXU_HMw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhA4w7o", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 113, "title": "Add English streaming ASR processor with real provisional and final TEXT outputs", "body": "## Problem

The extension currently has ReazonSpeech ja-en with `provisional: TEXT` and `final: TEXT`, but its English speech recognition is not satisfactory in user testing. The separate local Whisper tiny multilingual Node can transcribe English but emits **only `final: TEXT`**, so it cannot show continuously updated English transcription in `LiveTextDisplay.replace`. Add a third, **English-focused streaming ASR processor** that genuinely generates both outputs.

## Expected outcome

- Add a clearly named, model-specific Node, e.g. `SpeechToTextZipformerEn` (label **Streaming Zipformer English ASR**), backed by a real, local **English streaming Zipformer** or comparably appropriate sherpa-onnx online recognizer. Prefer an available pinned English model/runtime with practical Chrome Extension MV3 CPU-WASM size, latency, and memory characteristics. Verify actual model and runtime compatibility before settling on the package; do not ship a placeholder or cloud service.
- Ports: `audio: MONO_16KHZ_PCM` input; `provisional: TEXT` and `final: TEXT` outputs. Because this model is English-specific, do **not** add an unused `language` input. Connect `provisional → LiveTextDisplay.replace` and `final → LiveTextDisplay.append` in a supported example.
- `provisional` must originate from **real incremental recognition**, not replaying a completed transcript or fabricating partial updates. `final` must mark a completed/committed audio segment, without duplicate text or dropped tails when followed by new segments. Decide and document the supported end-of-utterance or segment-cap policy, VAD interaction, and any bounded buffering and backlog handling.
- Integrate a sherpa-onnx **online** recognizer runtime/Worker where required; the existing ReazonSpeech worker uses **offline** recognition, so simply swapping model weights into the offline worker is not sufficient. Preserve cancellation, graceful Stop/drain, repeated sessions, failure propagation, worker cleanup and model readiness.
- Extend `ASR_TYPES`, exactly-one-ASR graph validation, graph-editor searchable palette/typed ports/help, runtime assembly, session setup and model preparation. Preserve existing version 8 graphs, node IDs/routes/positions, saved ReazonSpeech/Whisper configurations, and all prior graph migrations. Leave the minimal default graph as ChromeTabAudio → ReazonSpeech → one LiveTextDisplay; users opt into the new English ASR via Graph Editor.
- Bundle/checksum-pin model assets and WASM runtime using the existing extension preparation/build processes, with offline availability and Chrome MV3 CSP compliance; **no remote inference or runtime downloads while recording**. Keep shared audio/output contracts and downstream formatting, translation, focused-field and Live sinks unchanged.
- Use real pinned English speech fixtures and deterministic segmented-stream fixtures to establish that the new Node actually emits meaningful **intermediate provisional events before final**, and English final results. Record relevant measured behavior (e.g. first partial latency, final delay, memory/runtime notes) and explicitly distinguish fixture tests from comparative English WER/CER or real-world accuracy guarantees.
- Document the English streaming model's provenance, artifact license/size, supported configuration, limitations, and how it differs from ReazonSpeech's simulated partial decoding and Whisper's final-only decoding. Avoid implementing a broad ASR SDK, dynamic model registry, multilingual controls or general-purpose streaming framework.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Model/runtime availability and license are confirmed; local, pinned online ASR loads from the packaged MV3 Extension without an inference network request, with the requisite preparation/build and CSP handling.
- [ ] Unit and real-model fixture tests demonstrate `provisional: TEXT` updated at least once **before** a `final: TEXT` for sustained English speech; a new utterance can start after a final without stale provisional leakage.
- [ ] Tests verify incremental audio ownership, ordered exactly-once final emissions, empty/no-speech behavior, utterance boundaries or segment cap, bounded backlog, Stop/drain, Cancel, failure cleanup, and repeat-session behavior.
- [ ] Graph Editor and runtime tests verify type-correct `ChromeTabAudio.audio → SpeechToTextZipformerEn.audio` and `provisional → LiveTextDisplay.replace` / `final → LiveTextDisplay.append`, plus compatibility with existing text sinks.
- [ ] ReazonSpeech retains both outputs and Number-configured maxDuration; Whisper remains **final-only**; existing saved graphs and migrations remain valid, without changing user configurations on reload.
- [ ] Document concrete model identity, online inference behavior, offline asset setup and limitations; run relevant unit, browser and packaged MV3 tests and extension build before merge. Report all skips and any optional real-world accuracy checks truthfully.

All mandatory acceptance checks must be achievable and verified before merge; no manual post-merge deployment step is a merge prerequisite.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

- `extension/graph.js` at Graph Version 8: `ASR_TYPES` currently covers only `SpeechToTextReazonSpeech` and `SpeechToTextWhisper`.
- `SpeechToTextReazonSpeech` has `provisional` and `final`; `SpeechToTextWhisper` now has only `final` following Issue #111, because Whisper's implementation has no real partial inference.
- Existing sherpa-onnx integration for ReazonSpeech uses offline recognizer logic (`web/sherpa-worker.js`). This new Node needs a genuine streaming recognizer, ideally an English Zipformer with a compatible online WASM runtime.
- This work is an **additional processor Node**, not a request to change existing recognition Nodes, add fake provisional ports, or change the default graph.
